messages:
leah (Support): Hi team — AcmeCorp opened a ticket: several users intermittently get an OAuth login failure when signing in with GitHub org SSO. They see a 403 on token exchange with an 'insufficient_scope' error even though the org app requests correct scopes. Repro steps + headers below from their support ticket.

customer-ops (AcmeCorp): repro steps we followed: 1) Click Sign in with GitHub 2) Redirect to GitHub SSO 3) Approve 4) Redirect back to https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback?code=XYZ&state=abc 5) Our app calls Redwood /oauth/exchange. Redwood returns 403 with body: {"error":"insufficient_scope"}. Happens for ~10% of users, random.

leah (Support): Customer pasted raw request show:

Request -> /auth/callback?code=abcd1234&state=st_98765
Headers:
  Cookie: redwood_session=eyJv...; redwood_session=eyJv_v2...; other=...
  Referer: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize

Server log (from our token proxy):
  WARN exchange failed for code=abcd1234, user=acct-42, err=403 insufficient_scope
  debug: token response scopes: [read:user] expected: [read:user,user:email,repo]

leah (Support): Note: the Cookie header contains two cookies with the same name (redwood_session) — one looks older (v1) and one new (v2). The proxy concatenates them which may pick the wrong session -> causes token exchange to use stale session that lacks requested scopes per customer.

kai (Eng Platform): thanks — can you add the exact Set-Cookie headers we previously set for this tenant? specifically Path and SameSite attributes. Also need the full token exchange request id (X-Request-Id) from our logs for 1744445555.

leah (Support): pasted from customer capture:
  Set-Cookie: redwood_session=eyJv...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Expires=Fri, 17 Jul 2026 12:00:00 GMT
  Set-Cookie: redwood_session=eyJv_v2...; Path=/auth; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Expires=Fri, 17 Jul 2026 12:05:00 GMT
  X-Request-Id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d

eric (SRE): interesting — second cookie has Path=/auth and SameSite=None. Some CDNs and proxies collapse duplicate cookie names differently (they may send first or last). If our auth service reads the cookie with Path=/ (older) it may not contain the latest token scopes. That would explain the intermittent nature (depends on which cookie wins).

nina (Security): could PKCE/state play a role? if the wrong session is used we might validate a different nonce and drop additional scopes at token refresh. We should verify code_verifier mapping for rwd-req-0a1b2c3d.

kai (Eng Platform): Agreed. Immediate mitigation: prefer cookie with longest Path match (i.e., /auth) for callback handler, or namespace cookies per release (redwood_session_v2_{tenant}). Long-term: change auth service to canonicalize duplicate cookie handling — pick newest Set-Cookie based on Expires or created-at header.

leah (Support): Customer tried workaround: clear cookies or use incognito and auth works reliably. They asked for steps to distribute fix to users — they want something server-side.

eric (SRE): Repro steps for us: emulate duplicated cookies in curl:

  curl -i -H "Cookie: redwood_session=OLD; redwood_session=NEW" "https://auth.redwood.ai/auth/callback?code=...&state=..."

Observe which cookie our service picked and whether token exchange succeeds. Also test with Path differences.

kai (Eng Platform): I'll open PLAT ticket and queue a small auth service patch to prefer cookies with more specific Path or later Expires. Hotfix candidate: if duplicate cookie names present, log a metric and prefer cookie with SameSite=None when handling OAuth callback.

deploy-bot: Created issue PLAT-12378 and linked to this thread (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/PLAT-12378).

nina (Security): also add a check to ensure code_verifier matches the session it's bound to. If mismatch, reject and surface more informative error to the client (don't return generic insufficient_scope).

kai (Eng Platform): assigned to @kai, ETA for hotfix: 48h. Will add telemetry so we can count how many callbacks see duplicate cookie names.

leah (Support): For now advising AcmeCorp: 1) Instruct affected users to clear cookies or use private window 2) If they have in-house proxy/CDN, ask them to preserve Set-Cookie order and avoid rewriting cookie names/paths 3) We'll roll out server-side patch — keep you posted.

customer-ops (AcmeCorp): thanks — we'll communicate the temp workaround. Please keep us updated on PLAT-12378.

eric (SRE): one more note — check load balancer sticky session config. If LB rewrites cookie or path for stickiness it can cause duplicate cookie name insertion.

leah (Support): marking this as escalated. Adding support reproduction checklist to the ticket: sample cookie header, X-Request-Id, incognito logs, and confirm payload for token exchange.

kai (Eng Platform): will post patch link here when ready.

leah (Support): thanks all :thumbsup:
